title: Daily Value: How to Tell Quickly Whether a Nutrient Is a Lot or a Little

seo.title: Daily Value: How to Read %DV Quickly
seo.meta_description: Percent Daily Value (%DV) shows how much one serving contributes to a daily reference amount. FDA’s useful shortcut: 5% DV or less is low; 20% DV or more is high.
seo.search_intent: Teach readers how to use % Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels.

excerpt: % Daily Value is a comparison tool, not a personalized prescription. As a quick FDA guide, 5% DV or less per serving is low and 20% DV or more is high.
content_html:
A label says 230 mg sodium and 10% Daily Value. The percentage often tells you more quickly than the milligrams whether that serving is a small or substantial contribution. %DV puts the nutrient amount against a standardized daily reference.

The fastest shortcut is 5 and 20

FDA’s rule of thumb is simple: 5% DV or less per serving is considered low, while 20% DV or more is considered high. Values between those points are moderate contributions rather than a special legal category.

Daily Values are reference numbers

Examples include 2,300 mg for sodium, 28 g for dietary fiber and 50 g for added sugars on a 2,000-calorie reference diet. The label uses those figures to calculate the percentage contributed by one serving.

Use the percentage differently depending on the nutrient

For nutrients many people are encouraged to get more of—such as fiber, vitamin D, calcium, iron and potassium—a higher %DV can be useful. For sodium, saturated fat and added sugars, a lower %DV can help keep totals in check.

It is not your exact personal requirement

Individual needs vary with age, sex, life stage, body size, activity and medical context. Use %DV as a fast label-comparison tool; use individualized advice when you need a personal target.

faq.question: Is 20% Daily Value high?
faq.answer: Yes. FDA uses 20% DV or more per serving as a general guide for a high amount of a nutrient.

faq.question: Is 5% Daily Value low?
faq.answer: Yes. FDA considers 5% DV or less per serving low as a general guide.

faq.question: Does 100% DV mean everyone needs exactly that amount?
faq.answer: No. Daily Values are standardized label references, not individualized prescriptions.
